item.title: New AI development in linear system identification
item.description:
New AI development in linear system identification

A new approach to kernel-based regularization for linear system identification has been introduced, focusing on stability-compatible kernels and non-Gaussian priors.

🔍 Overview

  • Kernel-based regularization uses positive semidefinite kernels to define RKHSs and as covariance models for stochastic impulse responses.
  • Sharp kernel conditions are known for RKHS stability, but almost-sure BIBO stability under Gaussian priors requires more restrictive conditions.

🧩 How it works

  • The new approach introduces stability-compatible kernels, which admit at least one stochastic realization with almost-surely absolutely summable sample paths.
  • Stability-compatibility holds if and only if the stable elements are dense in the associated RKHS, a condition weaker than RKHS stability.
  • Practical sufficient conditions, including a spectral criterion for stationary kernels, are derived.
  • Non-Gaussian priors are constructed to preserve a prescribed covariance while enforcing almost-sure stability.

⚙️ Key details

  • The approach yields a stable prior based on the stationary radial-basis-function (RBF) kernel, separating covariance structure from the mechanism enforcing stability.
  • Numerical experiments show substantial estimation gains for several important classes of impulse responses, with particularly pronounced advantages when relevant dynamics occur at late lags or in separated temporal regions.

💡 Why it matters

  • The new approach provides a more flexible and stable framework for linear system identification, with potential applications in various fields.
  • The separation of covariance structure from the mechanism enforcing stability offers a novel perspective on kernel-based regularization.
  • The practical sufficient conditions and the stable prior based on the RBF kernel could lead to improved estimation and modeling in various scenarios.

#AI #MachineLearning #SystemIdentification #KernelMethods #Stability

Source: Stability-compatible kernels: beyond Gaussianity for impulse response estimation

item.title: New Paper Proves Polynomial-Time Sparse Recovery with Diffusion Priors
item.description:
New Paper Proves Polynomial-Time Sparse Recovery with Diffusion Priors

A new paper addresses the limited theoretical understanding of using pretrained diffusion models as priors for ill-posed inverse problems. The authors provide a theoretical foundation for statistically and computationally efficient inverse solvers that utilize these models.

🔍 Overview

Diffusion models have transformed generative modeling by capturing and generating samples from complex data distributions. This success has led to interest in using them as expressive priors for highly ill-posed inverse problems in imaging and sensing. Despite strong empirical performance, existing theoretical guarantees are often asymptotic or entail prohibitive computational costs in the worst case. This paper studies sparse recovery from a small number of linear measurements, a classical problem in compressed sensing.

⚙️ Key details

  • Prior Model: The study assumes an accurate diffusion model capturing a sparsity-promoting Bernoulli-Gaussian prior.
  • Sensing Matrices: The results apply to a broad family of random and deterministic sensing matrices.
  • Sampler: A likelihood-guided annealed Langevin sampler is used to recover the sparse signal.

💡 Why it matters

  • Computation Time: The proposed method provably recovers the sparse signal in polynomial time.
  • Sample Complexity: The approach achieves near-optimal sample complexity.
  • Posterior Guarantees: When the signal is drawn from the postulated prior, the paper establishes total variation guarantees for posterior sampling after a final denoising step.

#DiffusionModels #CompressedSensing #InverseProblems #TheoreticalCS #MachineLearning

Source: Diffusion Models are Provably Efficient Priors for Sparse Recovery

item.title: Beep Locator: Using Claude Code to Triangulate a Mysterious Room Beep
item.description:
Beep Locator: Using Claude Code to Triangulate a Mysterious Room Beep

A box‑filled room in a house started emitting an intermittent beep; using Claude Code I built Beep Locator to pinpoint the source.

🔍 Overview

  • The system was created to locate a mysterious beep that began sounding a few weeks ago in a room full of unpacked boxes.
  • Claude Code generated the software, and the solution ran on a Python web server with a browser‑based UI.

🧩 How it works

  • A primary UI is served by a Python web application server.
  • Devices connect to the server via WebSockets after scanning a QR code or opening a URL. The UI requests microphone access.
  • Each listener records a 60‑second buffer of recent audio and runs a simple beep detection algorithm (see detector.js) that applies a Fast Fourier Transform and a high‑pass filter to find potential beeps.
  • When a beep is reported, the server selects the device with the lowest round‑trip time and has it play a short chirp.
  • The server then asks every listener to upload a clip spanning roughly 0.6 s before the beep to 0.8 s after the chirp. The chirp aligns the clips, a crucial step for triangulation.
  • The triangulated locations are plotted on a map; beeps appear as X marks and are logged in a “Sounds located” list.
  • Additional UI features:
    • Rough mode – manually drag device icons to approximate positions, which are then refined using the sound data.
    • Clapping mode – generate test sounds by clapping; these appear as diamonds on the map.

⚙️ Key details

Device Role
Two iPads Listener
Phone Listener
MacBook Pro Listener
Surface Ultra Listener
  • The system measures the interval between beeps and uses the triangulated positions to lock down the most likely source.
  • Reported accuracy was about 40 cm.

📈 Results

  • After the system identified the beep location, digging in the indicated pile of boxes revealed an ancient carbon monoxide detector that needed its batteries replaced.

📚 References

  • While building the project, Claude retrieved the 2007 paper “BeepBeep: A High‑Accuracy Acoustic‑Based System for Ranging and Localization Using COTS Devices.”

#Claude #AcousticLocalization #Python #WebSockets

Source: Locating the source of a mysterious beep with Claude

item.title: Performance Analysis of Component Selection in P300 Brain-Computer Interface Spellers
item.description:
Performance Analysis of Component Selection in P300 Brain-Computer Interface Spellers

A four-component full-factorial experiment using a public P300 dataset has identified that the effectiveness of brain-computer interface (BCI) speller components is conditional rather than additive. These findings challenge the conventional “all-on” approach to pipeline design for hands-free communication systems.

🔍 Overview

P300 BCI spellers are designed to provide hands-free communication for individuals with severe motor impairments. Researchers tested the performance of these systems by varying the inclusion of four specific pipeline components to determine how they interact and contribute to overall system efficiency.

🧩 How it works

The experiment evaluated components using mixed-effects models focused on accuracy, repetitions, and information transfer rate (ITR). The research tested the following four components:

Component Functional Role and Findings
Subject Calibration Identified as the strongest singular contributor to performance.
Euclidean Alignment (EA) Compensates for the absence of calibration in zero-calibration settings.
xDAWN Spatial filtering component tested within the factorial experiment.
Language Model (LM) Effectiveness depends on the strength of the underlying EEG pipeline.

⚙️ Key details

The study revealed several critical insights into how these components interact within a BCI pipeline:

  • Component Anti-synergy: Adding components that are independently useful can occasionally reduce overall performance.
  • Conditional Value: The value of specific components is not additive; their impact depends on which other components are present.
  • Language Model Constraints: Contrary to conventional wisdom, LM support is not universally beneficial, as its effect is strongly tied to the quality of the underlying EEG evidence.
  • LM Scale: Results from a larger language model showed a performance pattern similar to smaller versions.

💡 Why it matters

These findings suggest that BCI pipeline design should move away from maximalist “all-on” configurations. Instead, spatial and language-support components should be selected based on the quality of the available EEG evidence to optimize communication for users with motor impairments.

#BCI #Neurotechnology #MachineLearning #EEG #P300

Source: When More Is Not Better: Component Anti-Synergy in a P300 Speller
